description: Feed the routing engine REAL signal and filter the candidate pool, so Auto can actually differentiate models. This is the backend core of the task. Five coherent, dependent sub-parts, all in the Rust crates: (A) filter enumeration to chat-capable models using the provider's real metadata; (B) real per-model capability detection replacing uniform stamping; (C) real cost signal (seed bundled defaults, stop labeling paid cloud 'free') PLUS a per-model/per-family quality tier fed into AutoDefaultPolicy's quality-for-complexity ranking; (D) 404/unavailable-model resilience so Auto does not keep selecting a known-bad model and a mid-turn 404 degrades gracefully; keep it provider-general (not Gemini-only) wherever the signal generalizes. Do NOT rewrite the routing policy - it is sound; enrich its inputs. Do NOT regress working Ollama/Gemini enumeration, privacy routing, the thinking toggle, or chat affordances.
steps: == PART A: FILTER ENUMERATION TO CHAT-CAPABLE MODELS ==

In crates/providers/src/adapters/gemini.rs `list_models`, extend the private `ModelEntry` struct to also deserialize (all #[serde(default)], camelCase): `supported_generation_methods: Vec<String>`, `input_token_limit: Option<u32>`, `output_token_limit: Option<u32>`. These are the real fields the Gemini /v1beta/models response returns.

In `list_models`, EXCLUDE any model whose `supported_generation_methods` does NOT contain `generateContent` (nor `streamGenerateContent`) - a model that cannot do generateContent is not a chat candidate. This is the RELIABLE signal that removes embeddings (gemini-embedding-*), TTS/audio-out (*-tts, *-native-audio-*), transcription (*-transcribe*), image-gen (*-image, nano-banana-*), video (veo-*), music (lyria-*), robotics (gemini-robotics-*), computer-use, aqa, deep-research-*, antigravity-*. When the API omits the field entirely (empty vec) for a model, fall back to the name-family backstop below rather than dropping silently.

Add a small, documented name-family backstop helper (e.g. `fn is_non_chat_model_name(id: &str) -> bool`) that matches obvious non-chat families by substring (embedding, -tts, native-audio, -transcribe, image (as a suffix/segment, careful not to match legit chat models), nano-banana, veo-, lyria-, robotics, computer-use, aqa, deep-research, antigravity). Use it ONLY as a backstop when supportedGenerationMethods is empty/absent, so the primary signal stays the API's own methods list. Document each excluded family in a doc comment.

Keep the internal id-stripping (`models/` prefix) and displayName mapping intact. Carry `input_token_limit` (context window) forward - see Part B. Preserve the existing 401/403 error mapping and the key-in-header behavior (do NOT put the key on the URL).
== PART B: REAL PER-MODEL CAPABILITY DETECTION ==

Problem: `ModelInfo` has no capability fields, and `AvailableModel` gets caps via `instance.capabilities(&model.id)` (a per-model-string lookup) - so the adapter cannot see the /models metadata at cap time. Choose the cleanest of these and document the choice: EITHER (preferred) enrich `ModelInfo` in contract.rs with optional capability hints derived at list_models time (add #[serde(default)] fields such as `context_length` already exists; consider `supported_generation_methods`/modality hints) and have list_available_models prefer those over the string-based `capabilities()`; OR keep the ModelInfo->capabilities() path but make GeminiAdapter cache per-model metadata from the last list_models call so `capabilities(model)` returns real caps. Whichever path: the goal is that a Gemini model's Capabilities reflect its ACTUAL metadata, not a uniform stamp.

Replace GeminiAdapter::caps_for's uniform `streaming/tools/json_mode = true` and `model.contains` vision guess with detection grounded in the /models entry: set `max_context` from `input_token_limit` (Some, not None); set vision from known multimodal families (2.x/1.5 pro/flash are multimodal - keep a documented per-family map, not a claim that every model has vision); set tools/json_mode per what generateContent models actually support (document the per-family default; do not claim a capability a model lacks). Where metadata is unavailable, fall back to sane per-family defaults but never over-claim.

If you enrich ModelInfo (contract.rs), update its Default/new() and the frontend `ModelInfo` mirror + any fixtures ONLY if the field crosses IPC (ModelInfo does not currently cross IPC via AvailableModel, so confirm before touching the frontend). Update every ModelInfo construction site across the providers crate and its tests.
== PART C: REAL COST + QUALITY SIGNAL ==

COST fix (root cause of 'everything free'): in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs `pricing_table_from_config`, START from `providers::PricingTable::bundled_defaults()` (which already seeds nonzero cloud rates and zero local rates) and THEN overlay the persisted per-kind/per-model user rates on top (user overrides win). Currently it starts from PricingTable::new() (empty) so nothing is priced until the user types rates. After this, unknown cloud models get a nonzero default (not free) and genuinely-local kinds (LmStudio/Ollama/GenericOpenAI-loopback/Embedded) stay zero. Update/extend the existing test `list_available_models` cost tests and add a tauri-app test asserting a Gemini row is nonzero-priced with an empty user PricingConfig.

Confirm `bundled_defaults()` covers Gemini with a representative, documented, user-overridable rate (it already sets Gemini 1.25/5.0). Adjust the doc comment to state these are representative editable defaults, not authoritative vendor prices; the user-entered AppConfig rates override them (path already exists via PricingConfig).

QUALITY signal: add a lightweight, data-driven per-model quality tier so 'Prefer Quality' and complexity-aware Auto pick a stronger model for hard tasks and a cheaper/faster one for simple tasks. Add a `quality: f64` (0.0..=1.0) field (or a small `QualityTier` enum mapped to a score) to `AvailableModel` in builtins.rs (it is the IPC DTO both routing and the picker read). Resolve it from a small default per-family/per-kind tier map (e.g. pro-tier ~0.9, flash-tier ~0.6, flash-lite ~0.4, local models a middle ~0.5), keyed generically by kind + model-id substrings, kept overridable and NOT hardcoded to one provider. Document the map.

Thread the new quality field through EVERY AvailableModel construction site (compile-critical - hand-audit since providers may not build in-sandbox): the sole real builder in builtins.rs `list_available_models_with_build_errors` loop, plus test constructors in routing/src/signals.rs, routing/src/policies/auto_default.rs, routing/src/policies/manual_override.rs, routing/src/policies/registry.rs, routing/tests/demo_policy_extension.rs, providers/tests/demo_provider_extension.rs, providers/tests/net_peer.rs, orchestrator-core/tests/pipeline_e2e.rs, and any tauri-app tests that build AvailableModel. Give test fixtures sensible quality values.

In crates/routing/src/policies/auto_default.rs `quality_for_complexity`, BLEND the per-model quality signal into the existing capability/context proxy (do not discard the caps/context contribution; combine, e.g. weight the explicit quality tier and the caps/context score). Keep the complexity weighting (High weights quality more). Add unit tests: at HIGH complexity a higher-quality model wins over a lower-quality same-caps model; a PreferQuality hint picks the stronger model; PreferLocal still stays local; low complexity + cheaper still prefers the cheaper/adequate model. Ensure existing auto_default tests still pass (update fixtures' quality so the documented expectations hold).
== PART D: 404 / UNAVAILABLE-MODEL RESILIENCE ==

Ensure Auto does not KEEP selecting a known-bad model: because Parts B+C now give per-model real caps + quality + cost, current models (e.g. gemini-2.5-flash / newer pro) will out-rank stale ones. Additionally, if detectable at enumeration, FILTER models the Gemini /models response flags as deprecated/unavailable (check whether the entry exposes a deprecation/`description` marker; only filter on a reliable signal, else leave in and rely on ranking + error). Document what signal (if any) was reliably available.

Mid-turn graceful degradation: in crates/orchestrator-core/src/pipeline.rs run_turn, the routing decision -> provider -> stream path already emits MessageError + persists an Error-status message on a provider error (including HttpStatus 404). Confirm the 404 body (which includes Google's 'use models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview' suggestion) is surfaced verbatim in the MessageError message and NOT swallowed. Add/adjust a test proving a provider HttpStatus{status:404,...} error propagates to a visible MessageError with the body text intact.

OPTIONAL (implement only if clean, else document as deferred): an Auto fallback that, on a routed model's hard-unavailability (404), retries the turn with the next-best surviving candidate from the ranked list. If implemented, make it retryable and bounded (one fallback hop), and add a test. If it cannot be done cleanly without reworking run_turn's single-decision flow, leave it out and record the rationale in findings; the ranking + clear error is the accepted win.
== CROSS-CUTTING SELF-AUDIT ==

For any changed serde boundary type (AvailableModel gaining `quality`; ModelInfo if enriched), keep #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] and note the exact JSON key (quality -> `quality`) so FEAT-003 can mirror it in TS and fixtures. Do NOT change existing field names.

Run per-crate `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml --check` for providers, routing, orchestrator-core, tauri-app after edits. Where the crate compiles in-sandbox, run `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`; where it does not (providers/orchestrator-core/tauri-app per FEAT-001 findings), HAND-AUDIT every construction site and clippy-class issue (unused imports/vars, needless_lifetimes, dead_code, unnecessary_lazy_evaluations, flat-prose doc comments) so it lands in few CI rounds.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini `list_models` deserializes supportedGenerationMethods + inputTokenLimit/outputTokenLimit and EXCLUDES models lacking generateContent (embeddings/TTS/transcription/image/video/music/robotics/etc.), with a documented name-family backstop for entries missing the methods list; a wiremock test proves embeddings/TTS entries are dropped and a generateContent model is kept.

GeminiAdapter capabilities are per-model and grounded in metadata (max_context from inputTokenLimit; vision/tools/json per documented per-family truth), NOT a uniform streaming/tools/vision/json stamp; a test proves two Gemini models get DIFFERENT capabilities/context.

`pricing_table_from_config` seeds `PricingTable::bundled_defaults()` then overlays user rates; a test proves a Gemini row is nonzero-priced with an EMPTY user PricingConfig while a local (Ollama/LmStudio) row stays TokenPrice::ZERO.

AvailableModel carries a per-model `quality` signal resolved from a documented, generic, overridable tier map; every construction site (real + all tests across providers/routing/orchestrator-core/tauri-app) is updated and compiles.

AutoDefaultPolicy.quality_for_complexity blends the quality signal so at HIGH complexity a higher-quality model wins, PreferQuality picks the stronger model, and PreferLocal still stays local; new + existing auto_default unit tests pass.

A 404/unavailable provider error propagates to a visible MessageError with Google's replacement-suggestion body intact (proven by a test); Auto ranks toward current models and does not keep selecting a known-bad one.
cargo fmt --check clean for every touched crate; clippy-class and construction-site self-audit complete for crates that cannot build in-sandbox.
verification: Run `cargo test --manifest-path crates/routing/Cargo.toml` (compiles in-sandbox per FEAT-001) and confirm the new quality-ranking tests plus all existing auto_default/signals tests pass.
Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check`, and the same for routing, orchestrator-core, tauri-app; confirm exit 0.

For crates that build in-sandbox, run `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and confirm green; for crates that do not, document the hand-audit of every AvailableModel/ModelInfo construction site and the clippy-class review in findings so CI passes first try.
